title: Incident sidecar micro-playbook: compact handoff & postmortem surface for Console
creator: Marco Hernandez
description:
Summary:
This ticket proposes a compact, contextual 'sidecar' panel that surfaces during alert and incident flows in the Redwood Console. The sidecar is a small, persistent overlay attached to alerts, runbooks, and incident timelines that exposes: a minimal playbook (first-response checklist), on-call handoff info, one-click links to create or attach a postmortem, a micro-sparkline for relevant SLOs, and quick actions (ack, escalate, add note, open runbook).

Goals:
- Reduce cognitive load when responding to an incident by bringing the most relevant operational artifacts to the right context without leaving the alert or timeline view.
- Speed up handoffs between responders with a compact visual summary that includes last ack, current owner, escalation path, and links to the active postmortem draft.
- Make it trivial to capture a postmortem link / start a new postmortem from the alert flow.
- Surface SLO health at glance using a micro-sparkline and recent burn rate to guide prioritization.

Scope and constraints:
- UI-only prototype + annotated interaction spec; engineering dependencies listed in "decisions".
- Must render inside Console alert detail, incident timeline, and rollout-failure modals.
- Keep width <= 420px, support keyboard focus, and ensure 3:1 contrast on critical controls.
- Defaults to collapsed state on narrow viewports; expands on hover/tap.

User stories:
1) As an on-call engineer, I want to see a concise checklist and the escalation path next to the alert so I can react quickly.
2) As a team lead, I want a fast way to link the alert to a postmortem or start drafting one from the alert so nothing is missed.
3) As an SRE, I want a quick SLO trend indicator in the same context so I can judge whether to treat this as P0 or P1.

Prototype summary and flows:
- Collapsed sidecar: icon + badge (status, owner initials), opens to full panel.
- Full sidecar sections (top to bottom): header (title, alert ID, timestamp), status row (owner, last ack, duration), micro-playbook (3 bullet first-response checklist with checkboxes), SLO micrograph (7-point sparkline + recent burn rate tag), postmortem quicklinks (attach existing / start new), quick actions (ack, assign, escalate, add timeline note), links (runbook, PagerDuty/GH incident link, Confluence doc).
- Interaction notes: quick actions trigger API calls; starting a postmortem opens modal with prefilled context (alert title, id, timeline snippet).

Accessibility and localization:
- All actions must be reachable via keyboard (tab sequence defined in annotated spec).
- Aria-live region for critical status changes inside the sidecar (owner change, ack).
- Strings marked for i18n in spec.

Success metrics:
- 30% reduction in average time-to-ack for alerts where the sidecar is used (measured by feature flag cohort).
- >60% of incidents created from alerts have a linked postmortem within 48 hours (after rollout).
- Positive qualitative feedback from 5 pilot teams in usability sessions.

Notes for engineering: backend endpoints needed (examples):
- GET /api/v1/alerts/:id/context (owner, last_ack, runbook links, associated postmortem)
- POST /api/v1/alerts/:id/postmortems (create & attach draft)
- PATCH /api/v1/alerts/:id/acknowledge
- GET /api/v1/slo/:id/sparkline?window=1h
Implementation must support optimistic UI for ack/assign flows and expose telemetry for which quick actions are used.

Open questions:
- Should the sidecar be enabled by default for all alerts or gated behind feature flag? (PM recommends feature flag for pilot).
- For incidents spanning multiple alerts, do we show a combined playbook or per-alert sidecar? (Recommendation: per-alert sidecar with an optional aggregated view in the incident timeline.)

Design deliverables attached below and prototype links in "attachments".

Acceptance criteria:
- High-fidelity Figma screens for collapsed and expanded states across desktop and tablet.
- Clickable InVision/Protoflow prototype demonstrating: expand/collapse, ack, create postmortem flow, and SLO micro-sparkline hover details.
- Annotated interaction spec with keyboard order, aria attributes, and analytics events list.
- Design review notes incorporated and signed off by PM and 2 engineering reviewers.
comments: 2025-02-22 - Aisha: Initial sketch added to Figma. Moving to mid-fidelity after sync with PM.
2025-02-25 - Marco: PM review: prefer feature-flagged rollout and limit to 'alerts > severity P1' for pilot. Added to scope.
2025-02-28 - Joon (Eng): Need to confirm SLO sparkline endpoint latency. Suggest caching summary on alert record to avoid extra calls.
2025-03-03 - Priya (PM): Confirmed feature flag + pilot teams (payments, search infra). We want telemetry for create-postmortem rate.
2025-03-05 - Aisha: Updated prototype to include keyboard focus states and aria labels per accessibility review. Ready for engineering scoping.
decisions: Use a right-anchored sidecar pattern (max width 420px) to avoid blocking the main timeline.
Include SLO micro-sparkline with a hover tooltip showing 1h/6h/24h burn rates; source from slo-summary cache to avoid extra round trips.
Expose a lightweight 'start postmortem' flow that pre-populates title and timeline snippet and returns a postmortem ID to attach to the alert.
Roll out behind feature flag scoped to severity >= P1 for first 3 weeks; evaluate metrics before enabling wider.
review_feedback: PM (Priya): Add an explicit 'copy alert context' button for external incident reporters.
Eng (Joon): Replace live sparkline polling with on-demand fetch to limit signal when users repeatedly open the sidecar.
Security (Camille): Ensure postmortem creation respects RBAC & audit logs; added as dependency.
Design (Aisha): Add collapsed micro-state with owner initials + severity color for fast scanning in lists.
next_steps: Finalize annotated interaction spec and hand off to ENG for scoping (target: 2025-03-07).
Create feature flag configuration and rollout plan with PM.
Schedule usability sessions with Payments and Search infra teams during pilot window.
Track telemetry events: sidecar_open, ack_via_sidecar, postmortem_created_via_sidecar, sidecar_escalate
